record.paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
record.original_question: Suppose a ring R contains a one-sided nil ideal A. Must A be contained in a two-sided nil ideal of R?

evidence.quote: P2 (Koethe [4]) If a ring R contains a one-sided nil ideal A, is A contained in a two-sided nil ideal of R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be an associative ring (not assumed to have a unit, and not assumed to be commutative). A subset S of R is called nil if every element of S is nilpotent, i.e., for each s ∈ S there exists a positive integer n (depending on s) with s^n = 0. A left (respectively right) ideal A of R is a nil one-sided ideal if A is nil; a two-sided ideal I of R is a nil two-sided ideal if I is nil.

Question: Suppose R contains a one-sided (left or right) nil ideal A. Must there exist a two-sided nil ideal J of R such that A ⊆ J?
artifact.category_tag: Köthe conjecture / nil ideals in rings
artifact.status_search_result: This is a classical formulation of Köthe's conjecture (posed by Köthe in 1930). It is equivalent to the statement that the sum of two nil left ideals is nil. It has been verified in special classes (PI rings, right Noetherian rings, etc.), but the general problem remains open as of 2026. Smoktunowicz's counterexample to Amitsur's related polynomial-ring conjecture did not resolve Köthe's conjecture itself.

status_evidence.title: Köthe conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Posed in 1930 by Gottfried Köthe; equivalent to: every one-sided nil ideal is contained in a two-sided nil ideal.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is the classical Köthe conjecture, still open in general.

status_evidence.title: On some Results Related to Köthe's Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of partial results toward Köthe's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known; general case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:1510.07523
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work discussing Köthe's nil ideal problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem continues to be studied as open.
